content:
The paper "The Lean mathematical library" (written in 2019) includes this diagram of the typeclass hierarchy starting at normed_field. I was curious what it looks like nowadays, so I had my AI generate what it looks like in v32-rc1. With some prompting I added some interactivity, e.g. show fields added over parents.

I've been using it for a few days and spot-checked against the mathlib source code where I could, but please lmk if there are any inaccuracies (there were definitely some in the initial version written by the AI due to bugs in the pipeline)
This is neat! I've long wanted something like this built into the infoview or even just the online docs.
It seems that docs#NonAssocRing is missing from that graph, along with likely some others; is this intended?
The edge from docs#NonUnitalNormedRing to docs#NonUnitalRing is also missing

It seems that docs#NonAssocRing is missing from that graph, along with likely some others; is this intended?

I agree NonAssocRing should be in there. I believe it was not found by the pipeline because it's not directly extended by any other classes. Thanks!

I once vibe-coded Hierarchy builder for lean: https://github.com/spitters/lean-HB
It's the method rocq uses to avoid diamonds inheritance. Mathlib resolves them by hand (I understand). It's interesting whether this scales with mathlib growing, and with the development of other lean libs.

If I include all links like CommRing -> NonAssocCommRing, the graph is larger and harder to visualize. Probably what is needed is some UX innovations to selectively filter it down or otherwise make it easier to work with.

Nice!

In the paper I also included arrows from Prop-mixins to its arguments (e.g from docs#T0Space to docs#TopologicalSpace).
It might also be more readable if you omit the (thick) lines that follow from transitivity.
